customerDebt.metaTitle: Customer Debt Tracking — Balances and Payments
customerDebt.metaDescription: See what every customer still owes you, straight from your unpaid invoices. Record partial payments and know your total receivables. Works without internet.
customerDebt.intro: Selling on credit is normal. The problem is not the credit — it is losing track of who still owes you, and since when. Hisabche works each customer's balance out from your invoices, so there is no separate ledger to keep. To be clear: this page is about the credit you extend to your own customers — not bank loans or formal instalment finance.

sections.heading: Where the balance comes from
sections.body: Any sales invoice that has not been settled in full leaves a remainder — the invoice total minus what you have actually collected — and that sits against the customer. Nothing to add up by hand. One thing paper ledgers routinely get wrong: purchase invoices never enter this figure. What customers owe you and what you owe suppliers are two separate columns, and Hisabche keeps them that way.

sections.heading: Partial payments, not all-or-nothing
sections.body: A customer owes 100 and hands you 50. You record the 50 against the invoice; it stays part-paid and the rest still shows in your receivables. Same as crossing out and rewriting a figure in a notebook, except the history survives.

sections.heading: What you are owed, at a glance
sections.body: The dashboard shows total receivables next to sales and stock value. It is the number most shop owners never actually know — and usually the one that explains why sales look healthy while the till is empty.

sections.heading: When the connection drops
sections.body: Recording a payment or writing an invoice does not depend on the internet. You keep working offline and changes sync themselves once the network is back.

sections.heading: If you deal in more than one currency
sections.body: Each invoice is recorded in its own currency — AFN, USD, PKR or IRR — and you can filter the invoice list by currency. One thing to know: the dashboard’s total receivables figure currently adds every invoice together without converting between currencies, so if you genuinely trade in more than one, check the invoice list for that currency to get an accurate figure.

faq.q: Do I need a special invoice type for credit sales?
faq.a: No. Record the normal sales invoice and enter a received amount lower than the total. The remainder becomes the outstanding balance automatically.

faq.q: What if a customer pays in several instalments?
faq.a: Record each payment separately. The balance drops each time until the invoice is settled.

faq.q: Does this also show what I owe suppliers?
faq.a: As a separate figure, yes. Receivables and payables are deliberately not netted against each other, because they are two different things.

faq.q: What happens to my records if I lose my phone?
faq.a: Your data syncs to your account, so you sign in on another device and the balances are still there.

offline.metaDescription: Write invoices, adjust stock and record payments with no connection on the phone and Windows apps, then let everything sync to your account.
offline.h1: Work offline, sync when you can
offline.intro: Browser-based accounting tools stop working when the connection drops, and traditional installed software traps your records on one machine. Hisabche does both halves: the work happens on your device, and it syncs to your account afterwards.

sections.heading: Where offline actually works
sections.body: Full offline use is the phone app and the Windows app: writing an invoice, taking a payment, adding a customer and drawing stock down all happen with no network and are saved on the device. The web version is different — the browser needs a connection to save, and only shows you how many changes are still pending. If your shop’s connection is unreliable, install the phone or Windows app.

sections.heading: Syncing when the network returns
sections.body: Work done offline on the phone or Windows app is queued locally and sent in order as soon as you reconnect. There is no button to press and nothing to re-enter.

sections.heading: How this differs from old desktop software
sections.body: Traditional installed software is offline too, but the data lives on that one machine: you cannot reach it from a phone, and if the machine dies the records go with it. That combination — offline-first plus cloud sync — is the actual difference, not offline on its own.

sections.heading: Several devices, one account
sections.body: If you are on the till and someone else is in the stockroom, you each work on your own device, and after syncing everyone sees the same stock and the same balances — including from the browser.

faq.q: Does it work fully offline in the browser too?
faq.a: No. Full offline use is the phone app and the Windows app. The web version needs a connection to save.

faq.q: So I never need internet at all?
faq.a: Not for day-to-day work on the phone or Windows app. You do need to connect now and then so devices can sync and your records are backed up to your account.

faq.q: What if I stay offline for several days?
faq.a: The work queues up and is sent when you reconnect. There is no time limit on it.

faq.q: What if I sell the same item offline on two devices?
faq.a: Both sales are recorded and synced, and you see the true stock level afterwards. This is why it is worth syncing devices regularly when they share stock.

offline.ctaBody: Start free, and try the phone or Windows app with the network off.

shopAccounting.metaDescription: Run a small shop's books without an accountant: invoices, inventory, customer credit, a daily cash till and profit and loss, on web, phone and Windows.
shopAccounting.h1: Accounting software for small shops, built around how a shop actually works
shopAccounting.intro: Most small shops keep their books in a notebook or a spreadsheet, because accounting software is built for accountants. Hisabche starts from the shop's day — you sold, you bought, you gave credit, you got paid — and writes the double-entry records behind it automatically.

sections.heading: Everyday shop work, no accounting jargon
sections.body: Record a sale or a purchase, pick the customer, and say how it was paid: in full, partly (the rest becomes customer credit), split across methods, or not yet. Stock moves, the customer's balance updates and the journal entry is posted.

sections.heading: Stock, customer credit and the till in one place
sections.body: Every item shows its stock and the history behind it; low and out-of-stock items stand out. Each customer shows what they owe, with the invoices and payments behind it. The till is opened and closed daily and shows any difference between counted and expected cash.

sections.heading: Built for multi-currency and emerging markets
sections.body: Invoices can be written in Afghan afghani, US dollars, Pakistani rupees or Iranian rial, and the app works in English, Persian and Dari, with Gregorian, Iranian or Afghan calendar months to match.

sections.heading: Web, phone and Windows
sections.body: Sign in from a browser or install the phone and Windows apps; all see the same account. The apps keep working with no connection and sync when it returns.

sections.heading: Staff with limited access
sections.body: Invite a salesperson to the business as owner, manager or seller. Each role’s access can be changed in the permissions matrix — for example, a seller can record invoices without seeing profit and loss.

faq.q: Do I need to know accounting?
faq.a: No. You record sales, purchases and payments; the journal entries are created for you. An accountant can still read the same journal, trial balance and balance sheet.

faq.q: Which shops is it for?
faq.a: Small and medium retail and trade businesses with invoices, stock and customer credit — groceries, clothing, hardware, parts. Count, weight and custom units are supported.

faq.q: Does it work offline?
faq.a: Fully on the phone and Windows apps. The web version needs a connection to save.

faq.q: How much does it cost?
faq.a: You can start free. Plans are listed in the pricing section of the home page.

invoicing.metaDescription: Create sales and purchase invoices, print or download PDF, send customers a view link, and record full, partial or split payments on one invoice.
invoicing.h1: Invoice software that follows the money after the invoice
invoicing.intro: An invoice that only prints is half the job. You also need to know whether it was paid, what left the shelf and what went into the books. In Hisabche the invoice is where sales, stock, customer credit and accounting meet.

sections.heading: Fast entry from your stock list
sections.body: Pick items from inventory so price and unit fill in and stock drops on save. Lines not linked to an item, or a sale that would take stock negative, are flagged before you confirm.

sections.heading: Full, partial or split payments
sections.body: Say how the invoice was paid: in full, partly with the rest owed, or split across methods such as cash and bank transfer. Each method is its own payment with its own note, so the till and bank stay right. Later payments are added on the invoice itself.

sections.heading: Print, PDF and share links
sections.body: Invoices carry your business name and logo, print cleanly and export to PDF. Send a customer a link that shows that one invoice and nothing else.

sections.heading: Safe to retry on a bad connection
sections.body: Each invoice carries a unique request key, so a retry after a dropped connection returns the invoice that was already created instead of making a second one.

faq.q: Are invoice numbers automatic?
faq.a: Yes, each invoice gets the next sequential number.

faq.q: Which currencies can I invoice in?
faq.a: Afghan afghani, US dollar, Pakistani rupee and Iranian rial.

faq.q: Can I record a payment later?
faq.a: Yes, from the invoice page; the balance and the customer's credit update.

faq.q: Can I choose the invoice currency?
faq.a: Yes — Afghani, US dollar, Pakistani rupee and Iranian rial are supported.

invoicing.ctaBody: Start free — invoices, stock and customer credit are connected from day one.

inventory.metaTitle: Inventory Management Software for Small Shops
inventory.metaDescription: See every item's stock and the movements behind it, spot low stock, transfer between warehouses and run stock counts that update with every invoice.
inventory.h1: Simple inventory management that updates itself with every sale
inventory.intro: Stock numbers typed in by hand drift away from the shelf. In Hisabche the stock level is built from movements — sales, purchases, transfers, adjustments and counts — and every movement leaves a trace.

sections.heading: Every stock number has a history
sections.body: For each item you see which sale, purchase, transfer or adjustment changed it. Correcting stock from the item page records an adjustment instead of silently overwriting the number.

sections.heading: Low, out and negative stock
sections.body: Items at their reorder level show as low; zero or negative show as out of stock. Negative stock is never hidden, because it means more was sold than was recorded as bought.

sections.heading: Multiple warehouses and stock counts
sections.body: Move stock between warehouses and record periodic counts; the difference between the count and the system becomes an adjustment.

sections.heading: Units, weights and barcode scanning
sections.body: Track items by piece, kilogram or a custom unit, and scan barcodes with the phone camera in the mobile app.

faq.q: Does selling reduce stock automatically?
faq.a: Yes, when the invoice line is linked to an inventory item.

faq.q: Can I delete an item that has sales?
faq.a: No — items with sales or stock history are protected so past invoices stay intact. Deactivate them instead.

faq.q: Does stock update offline?
faq.a: On the phone and Windows apps, yes, and it syncs when you reconnect.

daybook.metaTitle: Daybook & Cash Book Software with Automatic P&L
daybook.metaDescription: Journal entries are created from invoices and payments automatically. See the trial balance, P&L and balance sheet, and trace any figure to its invoice.
daybook.h1: A daybook that fills itself, and reports you can trace to the source
daybook.intro: Small businesses either keep no daybook or re-enter everything at month end. In Hisabche every sale, purchase and payment writes its own double-entry journal record the moment it happens, and the reports come from those records.

sections.heading: Automatic journal entries
sections.body: A sales invoice records revenue and what the customer owes; a payment records cash or bank; a purchase records stock and what you owe the supplier. Moving money between the till and the bank is one balanced entry. Manual entries are available for anything else.

sections.heading: Trial balance, profit and loss, balance sheet
sections.body: All three are built from the same entries, and every figure drills down to the ledger lines and the invoices behind it.

sections.heading: Daily cash till and cash flow
sections.body: Open the till with a float, see cash sales, cash in and out and bank transfers, and close with a count that shows any difference. A 7, 30 and 90-day cash flow chart is included.

sections.heading: Budgets with commitments
sections.body: Set expense or revenue budgets per account; actual spend and open commitments are shown against them, with a warning or a block when a limit is crossed.

faq.q: Do I have to enter journal entries by hand?
faq.a: Not for sales, purchases or payments — they post automatically. Manual entries are for special cases.

faq.q: What about invoices created before accounting was set up?
faq.a: One button posts all unposted invoices; an invoice that already has an entry is never posted twice.

faq.q: Which currencies are supported?
faq.a: Afghan afghani, US dollar, Pakistani rupee and Iranian rial.

faq.start1Q: How long does it take to get started?
faq.start1A: Signing up takes a few minutes, and you can issue your first invoice straight after. No installation, no long training, no manual data migration.
faq.start2Q: Do I have to pay to start?
faq.start2A: No. The free plan has every professional feature and its only limit is 50 invoices a month. No card required.
faq.offline1Q: What happens when I have no internet?
faq.offline1A: Not for the desktop and mobile apps. There you can record invoices, customers and stock changes offline, and they sync when you reconnect. The web version needs internet.
faq.offline2Q: What if I record the same invoice on two devices?
faq.offline2A: Anything already synced is on the Hisabche server, so a broken device does not lose it. Changes not yet synced stay on that device — which is why it is best to sync whenever you are online.
faq.offline3Q: Is my data kept on the phone too?
faq.offline3A: Yes. A local copy lives on the device so that recording an order never stops, even if the server is unreachable.
faq.acc1Q: Do I need to know accounting?
faq.acc1A: When recording a sale, pick the customer and record the unpaid amount on credit. What they owe shows in accounts receivable and the customer balance report.
faq.acc2Q: Can I manage credit and debts?
faq.acc2A: Yes. Every credit invoice sits in that party’s file and each partial payment reduces the balance, so you always know who owes what.
faq.acc3Q: Can I record purchases as well?
faq.acc3A: Yes. Purchases and sales share one form, and their direction is kept apart — a purchase is never counted as sales revenue.
faq.sec1A: Connections to the server are encrypted, each business's data is isolated in the database, and every user can do only what their role allows. Important changes leave a trail.
faq.sec2A: No. You set a role and permissions per member, and can widen, narrow or suspend them at any time.
faq.dev1Q: Which devices does it work on?
faq.dev1A: Yes. The Hisabche mobile app is built for Android phones and designed to work offline.
faq.dev2Q: How many people can work at once?
faq.dev2A: Up to 5 users on the free and professional plans, and unlimited on the business plan.
faq.dev3Q: Can I run several shops separately?
faq.dev3A: Yes. Each business gets its own space and you switch between them without the data mixing.
faq.pay1A: The free plan is enough to get started. Each plan’s price and limits are in the pricing table on this page, read directly from the billing system.
faq.pay2Q: If I cancel, is my data deleted?
faq.pay2A: Yes — signing up starts a 7-day trial, no credit card needed.
faq.start3Q: Can I use Hisabche without accounting knowledge?
faq.start3A: Yes. You record sales, purchases and payments; Hisabche posts the double-entry journal entry for you. Reports are ready to read, and your accountant has full access to the ledger.
faq.offline4Q: What happens to my data if the internet goes down?
faq.offline4A: In the desktop and mobile apps, every entry is saved on the device and queued. Once you reconnect, the queue is sent to the server — nothing is discarded because of an outage.
faq.offline5Q: What if two devices change the same record at the same time?
faq.offline5A: Hisabche never silently overwrites one change with the other. The conflict appears on the Conflicts page so you decide which version stays.
faq.acc4A: Yes. Every sale, purchase and payment posts an entry with equal debits and credits to the general ledger, and the balance is enforced in the database. Profit & loss, balance sheet and trial balance are built from those entries.
faq.sec3Q: Is each business's data kept separate?
faq.sec3A: Yes. Each business has its own workspace, and that boundary is enforced in the database itself — a user of one business cannot see another business’s data.

getting-started.title: Getting started
getting-started.summary: From creating an account to your first invoice.

setup.heading: What you set up first
setup.body1: You are asked a few short questions: your business name, your language, and the currency your books are kept in.
setup.body2: Choose the currency carefully. Every amount is stored in the currency it was recorded in. You can change what you are shown later without anything in the books changing.
setup.step1: Create an account and confirm your email.
setup.step2: Set your business name and your books’ currency.
setup.step3: Add a few products or services.

existing.heading: If you already have data
existing.body1: Coming from paper or another program, the data-migration screen takes your file and shows a preview before anything is saved. Nothing enters your books until you confirm.

getting-started.seoTitle: Getting Started with Accounting Software — Guide
getting-started.seoDescription: Getting started with Hisabche: create your account, set your business name, language and currency, issue a first invoice and bring in existing data.

invoices.title: Invoices
invoices.summary: Sales and purchase invoices, your own columns, and recording payment.

kinds.heading: Sales and purchases
kinds.body1: Sales and purchase invoices are made from the same screen. What differs is the direction: a sale reduces stock and creates a receivable, a purchase increases stock and creates a payable.
kinds.body2: Saving an invoice updates both your stock and your accounts. There is nothing to post separately.

columns.heading: Your own columns
columns.body1: The invoice table has ready-made columns, and you can add your own — weight, purity, making charge, freight, or whatever your trade needs.
columns.body2: For every numeric column you decide whether it counts toward the total. A column that is on is added to what the customer pays; a column that is off is recorded for reference only.
columns.body3: A percentage column — a making charge, say — adds a percentage of the goods to the invoice. Several percentage columns add together.
columns.step1: On the invoice screen, open the table settings.
columns.step2: Add a column and choose its type.
columns.step3: If it should be charged, switch on “count toward the total”.

payment.heading: Recording payment
payment.body1: When you create an invoice you say how it was paid: in full, in part, by several methods — some cash and some by transfer — or not at all.
payment.body2: You can add or remove payments later from the invoice itself. Removing one cancels it and reverses its effect; the record stays for audit.
payment.body3: The paid amount on an invoice is always read from the actual payments, so the two cannot disagree.

invoices.seoTitle: Invoicing Guide — Sales and Purchase Invoices
invoices.seoDescription: How sales and purchase invoices work in Hisabche: one screen for both, your own columns, and recording full, partial or split payments.

customers.title: Customers and debt
customers.summary: Customer records, outstanding balances, and chasing what is overdue.

balance.heading: What each customer owes
balance.body1: A customer’s balance comes from their invoices and the payments applied to them. No separate figure is kept that could drift.
balance.body2: When a customer pays, you can say which invoice it settles, or let it clear the oldest debt first.

overdue.heading: Overdue
overdue.body1: A list of unsettled invoices with their age shows which debts have been waiting longest.

customers.seoDescription: Customer accounts in Hisabche: how each customer's balance is built from invoices and payments, and how to follow up overdue debts.

inventory.title: Inventory
inventory.summary: Stock on hand, multiple units, stock counts, and dead stock.

source.heading: Where the stock figure comes from
source.body1: Stock on hand comes from what actually moved — sales, purchases, returns, adjustments. It cannot be typed over, because then it would no longer match its own history.
source.body2: If a figure is wrong, the way to fix it is a stock count, not an edit. The count records the difference as an adjustment, so what happened stays visible.

units.heading: Multiple units
units.body1: If you buy or sell something in more than one unit — pieces and cartons, grams and kilos — you can define those units for that product and say how many base units each one is.
units.body2: One unit is the base, and everything is stored in it. You can also say which unit purchases default to and which sales default to.
units.body3: This is optional. A product with no units defined stays single-unit.
units.step1: Open the product and find the units section.
units.step2: Add the units and mark one as the base.
units.step3: For each other unit, enter how many base units it is.

insights.heading: Reordering and dead stock
insights.body1: Hisabche suggests what to reorder based on your real sales.
insights.body2: The dead-stock list shows what has not moved for a while and how much money is tied up in it.

inventory.seoTitle: Inventory guide — stock, units and stock counts
inventory.seoDescription: Inventory in Hisabche: stock on hand from real movements, buying and selling in several units, stock counts and reorder suggestions.

accounting.title: Accounting
accounting.summary: The ledger, entries, and where every figure came from.

automatic.heading: Posted for you
automatic.body1: You do not post entries by hand. Every sale, purchase and payment writes its own double-entry record.
automatic.body2: Every figure in a report can be traced to the entry behind it. Click a number to open the rows that produced it.

closing.heading: Closing a period
closing.body1: Closing a period locks its entries, so a report you have already taken does not change underneath you.

currency.heading: More than one currency
currency.body1: If you deal in more than one currency you can record the day’s rate. A rate belongs to its day, so past figures are read at the rate of that day rather than today’s.
currency.body2: You can switch what currency amounts are displayed in. That is display only — your books and invoices are untouched.

accounting.seoTitle: Double-Entry Accounting and the Ledger — Guide
accounting.seoDescription: Double-entry accounting in Hisabche: entries posted automatically from every sale and payment, period closing, and daily rates for several currencies.

pos.title: Till and shifts
pos.summary: Quick sales, opening and closing the till, and cash differences.

shift.heading: The shift
shift.body1: At the start of a shift you enter the opening cash, and at the end the cash you counted. If there is a difference, you are asked why.
shift.body2: The reason is required. A till that comes up short with no explanation is a shortfall nobody can account for later.
shift.body3: A closed shift is fixed and does not change afterwards.

pos.seoTitle: Point of Sale and Shifts — Guide
pos.seoDescription: Point of sale in Hisabche: quick sales, opening a shift with starting cash, closing the till with a cash count, and seeing any difference.

tills.heading: The till list
tills.body1: The till page lists every open and suspended till in one table: when it opened, how many hours it has been open, the number of sales and the cash that should be in it.
tills.body2: Expected cash is computed by the server from sales, cash in and out, and cash invoice payments, and cannot be edited — a figure you can type over is not a control.
tills.body3: Each person has one open till per branch at a time. Two open tills for one person are two counts that can never be reconciled.
tills.step1: Press «Add till» next to the table title.
tills.step2: Enter the opening cash and open the till.
tills.step3: Click a row to see that till's transactions in the table below.

cash.heading: Adding cash and profit %
cash.body1: «Add cash to till» records money put into the till with a reason. The reason is required so every amount can be explained.
cash.body2: Cash payments of invoices appear in the till's transactions automatically. Search and filters for in, out and invoices sit above the table.
cash.body3: Each cash receipt for an invoice shows the profit % of that sale, from the accounting core and the real cost of goods. When no cost is recorded, no figure is guessed.

closing.heading: Suspend and close
closing.body1: «Suspend» at the end of each row takes a till out of use: it accepts no sales or cash movements but keeps its money and history, and «Resume» opens it again.
closing.body2: «Close till» asks for the counted cash and shows the difference from expected cash before you confirm. A difference must be explained.
closing.body3: Closing records the handover figures as of that moment and posts the journal entry; later voids do not change a handover someone signed.

offline.title: Working offline
offline.summary: What works without a connection, and when it syncs.

devices.heading: On mobile and Windows
devices.body1: On the mobile app and the Windows version you can work with no connection. What you record stays on the device and syncs by itself once you are back online.
devices.body2: If the same record also changed elsewhere, you are shown the conflict and choose — rather than one silently overwriting the other.

browser.heading: In the browser
browser.body1: The web version needs a connection to work. If your power or connection comes and goes, the mobile app or the Windows version is the better choice.

offline.seoTitle: Offline accounting — working without a connection
offline.seoDescription: Working offline with Hisabche: record on the mobile and Windows apps with no connection and sync later; the web version needs a connection.

branches.title: Multiple branches
branches.summary: Running more than one branch, and reporting per branch.

branches.heading: Branches
branches.body1: You can run more than one branch and tie each employee to theirs. Reports can be seen per branch or combined.
branches.body2: A branch is a reporting boundary, not a separate security boundary — all branches of one business share one set of books.

branches.seoDescription: Running several branches in Hisabche: set up branches, tie each employee to theirs, and report per branch or for the whole business.

setup.heading: Setting up branches
setup.body1: Branches form a tree: a branch can sit under another, for example a head office with two shops below it.
setup.body2: All branches share one workspace and one ledger; a branch separates work and reports, not data.
setup.step1: Open Staff & payroll and go to the branches tab.
setup.step2: Add the branch by name and, if needed, choose its parent branch.

staff.heading: Staff and branches
staff.body1: Each employee can be assigned to one or more branches, so it is clear where they work.
staff.body2: Tills belong to a branch too: one open till per person per branch, so someone working in two branches has a till in each.

reports.heading: Reports by branch
reports.body1: Accounting reports such as profit and loss have a branch selector: view one branch or the whole business.
reports.body2: The combined report is the sum of the same documents the single-branch reports show; nothing is calculated separately.
reports.body3: Because every branch is in one ledger, a customer balance or supplier debt is one figure for the whole business, not per branch.

warehouses.heading: Warehouses
warehouses.body1: If each branch keeps its own goods, create a warehouse for each. The warehouse page lists warehouses with each one's total value, product count, low stock and out of stock.
warehouses.body2: A sales invoice says which warehouse the goods leave and a purchase invoice which one they arrive at. With a single warehouse it is chosen automatically.
warehouses.body3: Stock not yet in any warehouse shows in the «No warehouse» row and can be moved into the right warehouse without changing the product total.

permissions.title: Staff access
permissions.summary: Who is allowed to do what.

roles.heading: Roles
roles.body1: Each employee has a role, and the role decides what is open to them. A seller can sell but does not see the cost price; a manager sees financial reports; the owner sees everything.
roles.body2: You can see and change every permission in the access matrix.

sod.heading: Separation of duties
sod.body1: You can require that one person does not do both halves of a task — whoever raises an invoice does not also record its payment.
sod.body2: For a one-person shop, leaving this off is the right answer. A control that refuses the owner their own till teaches them to share a login, and that destroys every other control at once.

permissions.seoTitle: Staff Permissions and Access Levels — Guide
permissions.seoDescription: Staff permissions in Hisabche: what each role opens up, and how to require that one person does not both raise and approve a task.

assistant.title: The assistant
assistant.summary: Asking questions about your books, and what it can see.

what.heading: What it does
what.body1: You can ask about your business in your own words — who owes the most, what needs reordering, what this month’s sales came to.
what.body2: Answers are built only from the data in your own account.

limits.heading: What it cannot see
limits.body1: The assistant has no access to any other business’s data, and there is no way to ask it for any.
limits.body2: It cannot see your customers’ phone numbers, emails or addresses.
limits.body3: If the answer is not in your data it says so. It does not guess a number.

quota.heading: How many questions
quota.body1: Each account has a monthly allowance of questions. When it runs out, you are shown how to get in touch for more.

assistant.seoDescription: Hisabche's AI assistant: ask about your business in plain words, what the assistant cannot see, and the monthly question allowance.

data-and-backup.title: Data and backups
data-and-backup.summary: Exports, backups, and your data being yours.

backup.heading: Backups
backup.body1: You can take a full backup of your data whenever you want. The file is your actual data, not a list of headings.

export.heading: Exports
export.body1: Reports and lists can be exported to use elsewhere.

data-and-backup.seoDescription: Backups and exports in Hisabche: take a full backup of your data whenever you want, and export reports and lists to use elsewhere.

contents.heading: What a backup contains
contents.body1: The backup is a JSON file with the business's real data: customers, suppliers, products, warehouses, invoices and their lines, payments and their allocations to invoices.
contents.body2: It also holds stock movements (the source of product quantities), the chart of accounts, journal entries and lines, employees, branches and purchase orders.
contents.body3: Rows are written in a fixed order, so two backups of unchanged data are identical and can be compared.

limits.heading: Backup limits
limits.body1: Only the workspace owner can take a full backup, because it contains all of the business data.
limits.body2: It is an export, not a restore: there is currently no way to load it back into the app. It is for safekeeping, for your accountant, or for rebuilding by hand.
limits.body3: At most 5,000 rows per table go into one file. When a table has more, the file says exactly which table is incomplete — a partial backup is never silent.

csv.heading: CSV export
csv.body1: Lists and reports have an export button that creates a CSV file you can open in Excel or Google Sheets.
csv.body2: Each customer's statement exports with opening balance, debit, credit and running balance.
csv.body3: The export contains the figures you see on screen, from the server; nothing is re-added in the browser.
csv.step1: Open the page or report and, if needed, choose the date range.
csv.step3: Open the CSV file in Excel or another program.

offline.heading: Offline data
offline.body1: In the desktop and mobile apps, work done without internet is kept on that device and synced once it reconnects.
offline.body2: Until it has synced, that work is not in the server backup — make sure devices have synced before taking one.

barcodes.title: Barcodes and scanning
barcodes.summary: Several barcodes per product, scanning with a device or a camera, and scale labels.
barcodes.seoDescription: Barcodes in Hisabche: several barcodes per product, carton codes, scanning with a USB scanner or a phone camera, and reading scale labels on an invoice.

codes.heading: A product's barcodes
codes.body1: Each product has a main barcode, and you can add more: another supplier's code, a new packaging code or a carton code. Each code belongs to one product only.
codes.body2: An extra barcode can carry its own unit — scanning the carton code adds a carton, not a single item. Extra barcodes are recognised online; offline, only the main barcode.

scan.heading: Scanning on an invoice
scan.body1: The invoice and quick-invoice pages have a «Scan barcode» button. USB and wireless scanners work without drivers; on a phone or laptop you can turn on the camera.
scan.body2: A barcode that is on no product adds no row and says so; one that is on several products asks you to pick the right one.
scan.step1: On the invoice page, press «Scan barcode».
scan.step2: Scan with the device, or type the code and press Enter; or turn on the camera and hold the barcode in front of it.
scan.step3: The product is added to the invoice in the right unit.

scale.heading: Scale labels
scale.body1: A shop scale prints a barcode with the weight or the price inside it. With «Scale label» turned on in the hardware settings, scanning such a label adds the product with that weight.
scale.body2: When the label carries a price rather than a weight, the product's selling price is needed to work out the quantity; if it is missing, you are told and no row is added.

wallet.title: Business wallet
wallet.summary: Topping up the wallet and paying the subscription from it.
wallet.seoDescription: The business wallet in Hisabche: top up by card transfer or foreign currency, file the tracking number and receipt, and activate a plan from the wallet balance.

what.heading: What the wallet is
what.body1: Each business has one wallet, not each person: the balance belongs to the business and does not move when a colleague leaves. Each currency has its own balance.
what.body2: Only the owner, or a manager allowed to manage the business, sees the wallet and pays from it. Every movement stays in the history with its date and the balance after it.

topup.heading: Topping up
topup.body1: Payment methods are defined by Hisabche; each shows its own destination and instructions. Until one is defined, the page says so.
topup.body2: A top-up is a request: support checks the payment and credits the amount that actually arrived. Until it is approved you can withdraw it.
topup.step1: Open «Wallet» from the menu and choose a payment method.
topup.step2: Pay the amount to the destination shown.
topup.step3: File the amount, the tracking number and the date; card transfers also need the last four digits of the card. A receipt is optional.
topup.step4: Once approved, the balance shows on the same page.

pay.heading: Paying the subscription from the wallet
pay.body1: On the «Plan & Billing» page, choosing a plan offers paying from the wallet. Paying activates the plan at once, without waiting for review.
pay.body2: The plan price is set by Hisabche, and the balance must be in the plan price's currency. The wallet stays open after a subscription has ended, so you can renew.

developers.title: Developers and integrations
developers.summary: API keys, webhooks, selling from your own site, apps and a sandbox.
developers.seoDescription: Connecting to Hisabche: API keys with limited access, signed webhooks for events, selling from your own website with a public key, and a separate sandbox.

keys.heading: API keys
keys.body1: Each key is limited to this business and to the access you choose, and never exceeds its creator's own access. Keys belong to the business: all its managers see the same list.
keys.body2: A key is shown once. You can give it an expiry, revoke it at any time and see its use over the last seven days.

webhooks.heading: Webhooks
webhooks.body1: When something happens — an invoice, a payment, a product reaching its reorder level — Hisabche sends a signed request to your https address.
webhooks.body2: Reject a message whose signature is wrong or that is more than five minutes old. Failed deliveries are listed and can be sent again; an address that keeps failing is switched off automatically.

storefront.heading: Selling from your own website
storefront.body1: With a public key, your website reads products and stock from Hisabche and places orders. Prices and totals are always set by Hisabche, never by the site.
storefront.body2: A public key works only on the addresses you allow, and can only read the catalogue and place pending orders. Orders are confirmed by hand or automatically, as you choose.

apps.heading: Apps and the app marketplace
apps.body1: An app you build for other businesses connects to a business's data only with its owner's consent, and only with the access the owner approved.
apps.body2: Every new version is reviewed before it is published. A business owner can remove an app at any time.

sandbox.heading: Sandbox
sandbox.body1: Create a separate, empty business to test integrations: its invoices, stock and books are fully apart from your real accounts.

manufacturing.title: Manufacturing
manufacturing.summary: What a product costs to make, recording production, adding it to stock, and material cost changes.
manufacturing.seoDescription: Manufacturing in Hisabche: a product’s components and materials with your own columns, labour and other costs, the cost of one unit, adding the product to a warehouse, and a report of materials that got dearer or cheaper.

what.heading: What manufacturing is for
what.body1: Anything you make, assemble or prepare yourself — a device, a repaired part, a dish — has a recipe: what it is made of and what each part costs.
what.body2: One form serves every trade. You enter components and materials like invoice lines; pick them from your products or type a name freely, and add or remove any column you need.

make.heading: Making a product
make.body1: Every quantity is entered for making one unit. Workers, time, pay and other costs such as packaging or transport are optional. The cost of one unit and the total are worked out for you.
make.body2: You choose the currency, and each row has its own unit. If you set the total by hand you must say why; the calculated total is kept beside it.
make.step1: Open «Manufacturing» from the menu and press «Make a product».
make.step2: Choose the product, or create a new one, and set the currency.
make.step3: Enter the components and materials with quantity, unit and unit cost; add labour and other costs if you have them.
make.step4: Enter how many you are making and press «Record production».

stock.heading: Adding to a warehouse
stock.body1: At the bottom of the form is a switch, «Add to a warehouse?». Off, only the cost is recorded and no stock figure changes. On, you choose the warehouse — or create one right there — and the product is added to stock at its production cost.
stock.body2: You can also have the materials that were picked from your products taken out of the same warehouse. If a material is short, nothing is recorded and you are told so.

history.heading: History and report
history.body1: Each production stays in the history with that day’s components and prices; a material getting dearer later does not change what earlier production cost. A recipe that has been used gets a new version when you edit it.
history.body2: On each product’s page you see its manufacturing section and can correct it. The production report shows what was made in a period, which materials were used most, and whose cost went up or down.

recurring-invoices.title: Recurring invoices
recurring-invoices.summary: Issue the same invoice automatically every month or every few days.
recurring-invoices.seoDescription: Recurring invoices in Hisabche: make an invoice repeat when you record it so it is issued automatically every month or every few days; pause, resume and a history of every occurrence.

what.heading: What a recurring invoice is
what.body1: For things that are the same each time — rent, a subscription, a monthly contract — you need not write the invoice again. Record it once and say it repeats.
what.body2: On each occurrence the same invoice, with the same lines, is issued dated that day and unpaid; you record the payment yourself, as for any invoice. A purchase invoice can repeat as well.

setup.heading: Making an invoice repeat
setup.body1: The repeat is set when you confirm an invoice: the invoice on screen becomes the template. Choose «Every month, on this day» or «Every few days».
setup.body2: The first automatic issue is the next occurrence; the invoice you are recording now is this one’s. Setting up a repeat needs an internet connection.
setup.step1: Write the invoice as usual and go to the confirm page.
setup.step2: Turn on «Repeat this invoice automatically» and choose how often.

manage.heading: Pause, resume and history
manage.body1: On the invoices page, «Recurring invoices» lists your arrangements: each one’s next occurrence, pause and resume, issue now, and remove. Removing an arrangement does not remove the invoices it issued.
manage.body2: Every occurrence stays in the history — issued, skipped or failed, with the reason. If issuing fails several times in a row the arrangement is stopped and you are notified, so you can fix the cause and resume it.

business-analysis.title: Business analysis
business-analysis.summary: Collections, supplier delays, break-even and returning customers.
business-analysis.seoDescription: The business analysis page in Hisabche: overdue invoices to follow up, supplier delays and concentration, the break-even quantity of each product, and customers who return in later months.

collections.heading: Collections
collections.body1: This section lists sale invoices that are past due and still have a balance, most overdue first. Each one carries a suggested reminder tone: friendly, formal, firm or final notice.
collections.body2: The list is for your own follow-up; the app sends nothing to the customer. When it is empty, the page says whether you have no open invoices or none has reached a reminder date yet.

suppliers.heading: Suppliers
suppliers.body1: From your purchase orders it works out how many days, on average, each supplier delivers after the promised date and how many orders never arrived. A supplier with too few orders stays “unknown”.
suppliers.body2: If a large share of your purchases goes through one supplier, or a product is bought from a single source, it shows here. An order without a promised delivery date is left out of the delay measure.

breakEven.heading: Break-even
breakEven.body1: For each product it shows how many units must be sold, at the current gross profit, to cover the fixed costs of the range.
breakEven.body2: Recorded salaries are counted automatically. You enter other fixed costs such as rent yourself; until you do, the page says the figures are lower than reality.
breakEven.step2: Enter the other fixed costs for that range.
breakEven.step3: Compare the “break-even quantity” column with what each product actually sold.

cohorts.heading: Customer return
cohorts.body1: Customers are grouped by the month of their first purchase, and for each group you see how many bought again in the following months.
cohorts.body2: Sales without a customer are not in this table, and a month that has not arrived yet stays blank, not zero.

promotions.title: Promotions
promotions.summary: A percentage or fixed discount applied when a product is picked on a sale invoice.
promotions.seoDescription: Promotions in Hisabche: a percentage or a fixed amount off, for all or some products and customers, with an optional date range; applied to the suggested price when a product is picked on a sale invoice.

what.heading: What a promotion does
what.body1: A promotion is a rule that lowers the suggested price of a product when it is picked on a sale invoice: a percentage, or a fixed amount off each unit in a named currency.
what.body2: It can cover every product and customer or only some, always or between two dates. The seller can still change the price, and earlier invoices do not change.

make.heading: Making a promotion
make.body1: Managers and the owner make promotions. For a fixed amount you also choose the currency; such a promotion only applies to an invoice in that currency.
make.body2: If you choose specific customers, sales without a customer do not get the promotion. When several promotions fit one product only the largest applies, unless you turned on “Add to other promotions”.
make.step1: On the Promotions page, press “New promotion”.
make.step2: Enter the name, type and value, and limit it to products, customers or dates if needed.
make.step3: Save; from then on a covered product shows a “Promo” tag on the sale invoice.

retire.heading: Changing or ending a promotion
retire.body1: A promotion is not edited or deleted; you retire it and make a new one if needed. That way the price on an old invoice can always be explained.

lists.heading: Price lists
lists.body1: A price list is a set of special prices in one currency, for example “Wholesale”. A customer on the list is offered those prices when a product is picked on a sale invoice, and the list name shows beside the product.
lists.body2: A product that is not on the list sells at its own price, the list only applies to an invoice in the same currency, and promotions are taken off the list price. A customer is on one list only.

installments.title: Invoice installments
installments.summary: Split the balance of a sale invoice into monthly parts.
installments.seoTitle: Guide to invoice installments in Hisabche
installments.seoDescription: Invoice installments in Hisabche: split the balance of a sale invoice into equal monthly parts and see which part is paid and which is overdue.

what.heading: What installments are
what.body1: When a customer pays the balance of an invoice over several months, you can split that balance into monthly parts so each part has its own due date.
what.body2: An installment plan is only a schedule. Payments are still recorded with “Record payment”, and the plan itself charges no fee.

make.heading: Splitting an invoice
make.body1: The current balance is split into equal parts and the rounding remainder goes on the first one, so the parts add up to exactly the balance.
make.step1: Open the sale invoice and show the “Installments” section.
make.step2: Choose the number of parts and the due date of the first one.
make.step3: Press “Split into installments”. Later parts fall on the same day of each following month.

follow.heading: Following the parts
follow.body1: Each payment recorded for the invoice is taken off the oldest part first. The table shows which part is paid, which is not due yet and which is overdue by how many days.
follow.body2: You can remove the plan; recorded payments are not touched.

lateFees.heading: Late fees
lateFees.body1: If a manager has turned the late fee rule on, the “Late fee” section of an invoice shows what is past due and what fee can be charged: a fixed amount for every 30 full days late, or a percentage of the overdue amount.
lateFees.body2: A fee is never charged automatically; a manager charges it, and a separate sale invoice is issued to the same customer. The fee is worked out on the unpaid amount, not the whole invoice, and each period is charged only once.

attendance.title: Attendance
attendance.summary: The daily sheet of check-ins, check-outs, leave and absence.
attendance.seoTitle: Guide to employee attendance in Hisabche
attendance.seoDescription: Attendance in Hisabche: a daily sheet to record each employee’s check-in and check-out, leave and absence, with hours worked and the count of present and absent staff.

sheet.heading: The daily sheet
sheet.body1: In “Team and payroll”, the “Attendance” tab shows every employee for one day. Managers and the owner see and record it.
sheet.body2: Each employee has one row per day; recording again corrects that row.
sheet.step2: For each employee press “Check in now”, or type the time.
sheet.step3: When they leave press “Check out now”; or record leave or absence.

meaning.heading: What the figures mean
meaning.body1: An employee with nothing recorded is “not recorded”, not absent. A day with a check-in and no check-out stays “not checked out yet” and shows no hours.
meaning.body2: Attendance does not change anyone’s pay automatically.

ai-assistants.title: Connect an AI assistant (MCP)
ai-assistants.summary: Connect Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini or Cursor to Hisabche over the MCP protocol.
ai-assistants.seoTitle: Connect an AI assistant to Hisabche with MCP
ai-assistants.seoDescription: How to connect Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini and Cursor to Hisabche over MCP: creating an API key, the connection address, the available tools, and human approval for financial actions.

what.heading: What MCP is in Hisabche
what.body1: MCP is a standard protocol AI assistants use to connect to software. With it you can ask your assistant which customer owes money, how much of a product is in stock, or to find an invoice.
what.body2: The assistant works through the same public API of Hisabche: the same key, the same access and the same rules. It has no separate way into your data, and sees only the business the key belongs to.

connect.heading: Connecting an assistant
connect.body1: The connection uses an API key that you create and can revoke at any time. Limit the key to what the assistant needs — for example, only reading customers and invoices.
connect.body2: The connection address is shown on the Developers page, in the “AI assistants” section.
connect.step1: On the Developers page, create an API key with the access you need.
connect.step2: In your assistant, add an HTTP MCP connection and enter the connection address.
connect.step3: Put the key in that connection as an Authorization header with a Bearer value.
connect.step4: Ask the assistant to list its tools; it sees only the tools the key allows.

safety.heading: Safety and human approval
safety.body1: Reading, and low-risk actions such as adding a customer, are carried out directly. Actions that move money or stock or cannot be undone — issuing an invoice, confirming, fulfilling and cancelling an order — are not carried out when the assistant asks.
safety.body2: Such a request waits in the approval queue until a manager or the owner approves or rejects it inside Hisabche. On approval the action is done in that person’s name, once. A request left unanswered for a day can no longer be approved.
safety.body3: An assistant cannot approve on your behalf, see another business, or reach the database directly.

tools.heading: Available tools
tools.body1: Searching and reading customers, products, warehouse stock, invoices, payments, orders and the customer debt report; creating and editing a customer; placing an order; and requesting an invoice or a change of an order’s state.
tools.body2: Every list returns at most 50 rows per page. Each call the assistant makes is recorded in that key’s usage log.

campaigns.title: Customer campaigns and surveys
campaigns.summary: Send a message or an NPS survey by email to a group of customers.
campaigns.seoTitle: Guide to email campaigns and NPS surveys in Hisabche
campaigns.seoDescription: Campaigns in Hisabche: send a message or an NPS survey by email to every customer, those with overdue invoices, recent buyers or inactive customers, and see the delivery state and the NPS score.

what.heading: What a campaign is
what.body1: A campaign is one email sent to a group of your own customers: all of them, those with an overdue invoice, those who bought recently, or those who have not bought for a while.
what.body2: There are two kinds: a “message”, which is only your text, and an “NPS survey”, which asks under your text how likely the customer is to recommend you.

send.heading: Sending a campaign
send.body1: Before sending you see how many customers will get the email and how many will not — because they have no email address or asked not to be written to. Sending takes a separate confirmation.
send.body2: Once sent, a campaign is no longer edited. The state of each email is what the mail service reports: in the queue, sent, or not delivered.
send.step1: On the Campaigns page press “New campaign” and choose the type, the group and the language.
send.step2: Write the subject and the text; wherever you write {name} the customer’s name appears.
send.step3: Save the draft and look at the audience count.

nps.heading: The NPS survey
nps.body1: From the link in the email, with no account, the customer gives a score from 0 to 10 and may say why. Each customer answers once, and the survey can be answered for 60 days.
nps.body2: Scores of 9 and 10 are “promoters”, 7 and 8 “passives”, and 0 to 6 “detractors”. The NPS is the share of promoters minus the share of detractors.
nps.body3: Beside the score you always see how many people answered. Until somebody answers, no score is shown.

optout.heading: Opting out
optout.body1: Every email carries an “I do not want these messages” link. A customer who uses it is left out of later campaigns, and that shows in the campaign’s report.
